message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition; take photos or videos. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep premises in good repair and free of health hazards. | • Report problems promptly; keep written records. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to fix major repairs within 30 days after notice, tenant may withhold rent or pay for repairs and deduct cost. | • Document all communications. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenant has the right to live without unreasonable interference from landlord or other tenants. | • Landlord cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24 hours). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal: 60 days before lease end.
• For termination due to nonpayment: 3 days notice if lease is month‑to‑month. | • Written notice is required; keep copies. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow court procedures; cannot forcibly remove tenant.
• Eviction requires a valid reason (nonpayment, lease violation, etc.) and a court order. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for month‑to‑month agreements.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions (e.g., banning pets unless justified). | • Review lease carefully; negotiate terms. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does not have statewide rent control; however, local ordinances may apply in certain cities. | • Check city regulations. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • If landlord fails to repair within 30 days after notice, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent. | • Keep receipts and proof of payment. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep written records of all communication with your landlord, including emails, texts, and written notices. Take photos or videos of any maintenance issues. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code, especially Chapters 24 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law) and 12 (Fair Housing). 3. **Use Written Notices** – When reporting problems or giving notice to vacate, use written notices and keep copies. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you face eviction or believe your landlord is violating your rights, consult a tenant‑rights organization or attorney. Many nonprofits offer free or low‑cost legal aid. 5. **File Complaints** – If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Security deposit returned within 30 days after lease ends. - [ ] Landlord maintains plumbing, heating, electrical, structure, and pest control. - [ ] Landlord gives 24‑hour notice before entering. - [ ] Landlord follows proper eviction procedure (court order). - [ ] Landlord does not discriminate. - [ ] Lease is in writing for month‑to‑month agreements. If you need more detailed guidance or help drafting a lease or notice, let me know!
